paragraphs.text: It must needs be a matter of some rare and marvellous consequence, that "Behold" - the "oh yes!" of the Holy Ghost - is thus set before.
paragraphs.anchor: Behold the Lord emptieth.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Will empty; an idiom proper to God’s prophets, who saw in the Spirit things to come as if they were even then done.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord emptieth

paragraphs.text: Or, The land, sc., Of Jewry, by a woeful desolation, Lege et luge, by law and lament. Some hold it to be a metaphor from ships overloaded, which therefore must be disburdened; so was the land to be eased of her inhabitants, which she could hardly stand under.
paragraphs.anchor: The earth.

paragraphs.text: Making havoc of persons and things of worth.
paragraphs.anchor: And waste.

paragraphs.text: Ferens, agens sursum deorsum omnia, turning all things topsy turvy, as they say.
paragraphs.anchor: Turneth it upside down.

paragraphs.text: Or, Prince. Dignity and wealth hindereth him not; doth he esteem nobility or riches, or anything that fortifieth strength? Poverty or meanness findeth no favour with him. In a common calamity, all commonly share and fare alike.
paragraphs.anchor: And it shall be, as with the people, so with the priest.

paragraphs.text: See on Isa 24:1.
paragraphs.anchor: The land shall be utterly emptied.

paragraphs.text: And his words are not in vain. Doth he say, and shall he not do it? {Num 23:23}
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord hath spoken this word.

paragraphs.text: Luxit et diffiuxit, waileth and faileth; gallant rhetoric in the original, as this is a stately chapter all along: all the rollings of Demosthenes are but dull stuff compared to it.
paragraphs.anchor: The earth mourneth and fadeth away.

paragraphs.text: As a sick man, so enfeebled that he cannot stand high alone.
paragraphs.anchor: The world languisheth.

paragraphs.text: {a} viz., With sin, and therefore so decayed; yea, the very visible heavens are defiled with man’s sin, and shall therefore be purged by the fire of the last day; like as the vessels that held the sin-offering was to pass the fire.
paragraphs.anchor: The earth also is defiled

paragraphs.text: Natural and moral; those bounds and banks set to keep men within the compass of obedience: "but the unjust knoweth no shame," {Zep 3:5} is lawless, aweless, yokeless, untameable, untractable as the wild ass colt, as the horse and mule, &c.
paragraphs.anchor: Because they have transgressed the laws.

paragraphs.text: Or, Passed by the ordinances - sc., by sins of omission, as before by commission; so in Heb 2:2, "every transgression and disobedience," i.e., every commission and omission.
paragraphs.anchor: Changed the ordinances.

paragraphs.text: Disannulled, vacated the covenant founded in Christ, when coming unto his own, his own received him not; when the Pharisees and others, by slighting holy offers and ordinances of grace, "rejected the counsel of God against themselves." {Luk 7:30} This last especially brought the curse. {Isa 24:6} Some by laws here understand the judicial laws, by ordinances the ceremonial, and by everlasting covenant the Decalogue. Others by laws, the municipal laws of the commonwealth, by ordinances the laws of nations, as not to violate an ambassador, &c., by everlasting covenant the law of nature, which is that "light that lighteneth every man that cometh into the world." {Joh 1:9}
paragraphs.anchor: Broken the everlasting covenant.

paragraphs.text: {a} Nempe contactu sceleratorum hominum. - Pisc.

The Chaldee and Vatablus render it the perjury - viz., in transgressing the laws, &c., which they had covenanted and sworn to observe; see Psa 119:106. That dreadful curse of the Jews {Mat 27:25} is come upon them to the utmost, devouring their land and desolating the inhabitants thereof. Though the curse causeless come not, yet God sometimes saith Amen to other men’s curses, as he did to Jotham’s upon the Shechemites. {Jdg 9:57} How much more to men’s cursing themselves?
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore hath the curse devoured the earth.

paragraphs.text: As being spilled and spoiled by the enemy.
paragraphs.anchor: The new wine mourneth.

paragraphs.text: Who were wont to sing away care, and to call for their cups.
paragraphs.anchor: All the merry hearted do sigh.

paragraphs.text: Quicquid laetitiarum fuit, in luctum vertitur.
paragraphs.anchor: The mirth of tabrets ceaseth.

paragraphs.text: Revel it as they had wont to do: non convivabuntur pergraecando. We use to call such merry griggs - that is, Greeks.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall not drink wine with a song.

paragraphs.text: Urbs desolanda, destined to desolation: whether it be Babylon, Tyre, Jerusalem, or any other. Mundum intellige in quo nihil nisi vanum, saith Oecolampadius: that is, by this city of vanity - so the Vulgate translateth it - understand the world; according to that of the preacher, "Vanity of vanities, all is vanity." Augustine, in the beginning of that excellent work of his, De Civitate Dei, maketh two opposite cities - the one the city of God, the other the city of the devil; the one a city of verity, the other a city of vanity.
paragraphs.anchor: The city of confusion.

paragraphs.text: The drunkards weep, the ale stakes yell, because the new wine is cut off from their mouths. {Joe 1:5}
paragraphs.anchor: There is a crying for wine.

paragraphs.text: Heb., It is eventide with joy. As the air in the evening waxeth dark, so shall their mirth be turned into heaviness.
paragraphs.anchor: All joy is darkened.

paragraphs.text: Together with their liquor. Wine is by Simonides called the expeller of sadness - Aμυντωρ δυσφροσυναων..
paragraphs.anchor: The mirth of the land is gone.

paragraphs.text: There is nothing of any worth left, but havoc made of all; it is plundered to the life, as now we phrase it. Since the Swedish wars custom is the sole mint master of current words.
paragraphs.anchor: In the city is left desolation.

paragraphs.text: Or, For so it shall be in the land among the people, as in the beating of an olive tree, &c. En misericordiae specimen, still there is a remnant reserved for royal use; quando omnia passim pessum eunt. God never so punisheth but he leaveth some matter for his mercy to work upon. A church on earth he will ever have.
paragraphs.anchor: When thus it shall be in the midst of the land.

paragraphs.text: Laudabunt Deum et laetabuntur: this elect remnant in all countries shall be filled with spiritual joy and peace through the belief of the truth, which shall vent itself by singing praises to God. And here we have the very mark of the true Church, which is to celebrate and profess the great and glorious name of the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall lift up their voice, &c.

paragraphs.text: Or, For the magnificence; that great work of his especially of divulging his gospel all the world over, and thereby gathering his Church out of all nations.
paragraphs.anchor: For the majesty of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: i.e., From the islands and transmarine parts, as we do now from Great Britain - "thanks be unto God for his unspeakable gift" - calling to our neighbour nations, and saying,
paragraphs.anchor: They shall cry aloud from the sea

paragraphs.text: In ipsis ignibus, in the hottest fires of afflictions, "rejoice in hope, be patient in tribulation"; praise God for crosses also: this is Christianorum propria virtus, saith Jerome.
paragraphs.anchor: Glorify ye God in the fires.

paragraphs.text: Quicunqui quocunque loco, et inter quoseunque sitis. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: In the isles of the sea.

paragraphs.text: {a} Jun.
Or, Psalms, aliquid Davidicam. The martyrs sang in the fire. Luther in deep distress called for the 46th Psalm to be sung in contemptum diaboli, in despite of the devil.
paragraphs.anchor: From the uttermost part of the land have we heard songs.

paragraphs.text: To Jesus the Just One. {1Jn 2:2}
paragraphs.anchor: Even glory to the righteous.

paragraphs.text: The prophet’s flesh was wasted and consumed with care and grief {a} for his graceless countrymen. See the like in David {Psa 119:158} and Paul. {Rom 9:1-2}
paragraphs.anchor: But I said, My leanness, my leanness.

paragraphs.text: Or, Alas for me.
paragraphs.anchor: Woe unto me.

paragraphs.text: They have crucified the Lord of glory upon a desperate and deep malice, out of most notorious contumacy and ingratitude. This was with most treacherous treachery to deal treacherously; this was to "do evil as they could."
paragraphs.anchor: The treacherous dealers have dealt treacherously.

paragraphs.text: {a} Merore ac macie conficior.

Metaphora a venatoribus, a metaphor from hunters, elegantly expressed in the original by words of a like sound. God hath variety of plagues at command; his quiver is full of shafts, neither can he possibly want a weapon to beat his rebels with. If the Amorites escape the sword, yet they are brained with hailstones {Jos 10:11} If the Syrians get into a walled town, yet they are baned by the fall of a wall upon them. {1Ki 20:30}
paragraphs.anchor: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee.

paragraphs.text: See Amo 5:19. {See Trapp on "Amo 5:19"} And learn to fear God, the stroke of whose arm none may think to escape.
paragraphs.anchor: He who fleeth from the noise of the fear.

paragraphs.text: The cataract or sluices of the clouds, as once in the general deluge.
paragraphs.anchor: For the windows from on high are opened.

paragraphs.text: Heaven and earth shall fight against them, and conspire to mischieve them.
paragraphs.anchor: The foundations of the earth do shake.

paragraphs.text: This he had said before. Oil, if not well rubbed in, pierceth not the skin. Menaces must be inculcated, or else they will be but little regarded. Let preachers press matters to the utmost, drive the nail home to the head; not forbearing through faint-heartedness, nor languishing through lukewarmness.
paragraphs.anchor: The earth is utterly broken down.

paragraphs.text: As the inhabitants thereof had drunk in iniquity like water; {Job 15:16} so they should now drink and be drunk with the cup of God’s wrath.
paragraphs.anchor: The earth shall reel to and fro like a drunkard.

paragraphs.text: Or, Lodge, hut, or tent; so shall they be tossed and tumbled from one place to another.
paragraphs.anchor: And shall be removed like a cottage.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The punishment of your transgression. Observe here the wages and the weight of sin.
paragraphs.anchor: And the transgression

paragraphs.text: Altitudinis in excelso. Hereby he may mean the Jews, God’s "firstborn, and therefore higher than the kings of the earth," {Psa 89:27} though now for most part degenerated, and therefore in the next words also heavily threatened, for versum vicesimum primum secundus explicat, saith Scultetus.
paragraphs.anchor: The Lord shall punish the host of the high ones that are on high.

paragraphs.text: Id quod de poenis Iudaeorum intelligimus, saith an interpreter - that is, This we understand to be the punishment of the obstinate Jews, whose bodies after death were clapped up close prisoners in the grave, their souls held fast in hell till the last day; when after many days they shall be visited, i.e., in the whole man punished with eternal torments. Caveamus, si sapimus, a destinata peccandi malitia. Origen was certainly out when he argued from his text, that the damned in hell should after a time be visited, that is, delivered. There are that begin the promise at these words,
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall be gathered together, &c.

paragraphs.text: i.e., In mercy and favour {as Isa 23:17} through Christ. This gracious visitation began in Israel, {Luk 1:68} and then came abroad to the Gentiles also. {Act 15:14-17}
paragraphs.anchor: And after many days shall they be visited

paragraphs.text: The glory of Christ’s kingdom shall be so great, that in comparison to it the sun and moon shall cast no light. See Isa 24:23; Isa 60:19.
paragraphs.anchor: Then the moon shall be confounded.

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ, summus caelitum Imperator.
paragraphs.anchor: When the Lord of hosts.

paragraphs.text: The whole Church and especially her officers, which are the glory of Christ. {2Co 8:23}
paragraphs.anchor: And before his ancients.
